title: migrateMint inflates id-6 supply with zero on-chain assertion that NFTStakerV2 reward runway has been topped up — early migrators can dilute existing id-6 stakers' yield if deployment ordering is off
out_of_scope_rationale: Out of scope per user scope guidance for this run. The vulnerability depends on (a) NFTStakerV2 — explicitly marked OOS by the user ('Findings about NFTStakerV2 missing or being incomplete are out of scope'), and (b) the cross-repo deployment broadcast script in phoenix-phase-2-staging — also explicitly OOS ('Findings about the deployment broadcast script being absent are out of scope'). The user's framing: 'It's not the job of yield-claim-nft to do everything, just its part.' The yield-claim-nft side exposes a migration entry point; sequencing the broadcast and funding the staker is the staging-repo / operator's responsibility. The on-chain gap inside migrateMint (no coupling to downstream staker solvency) is real but yield-claim-nft is not the right contract to enforce it — coupling to NFTStakerV2 from BalancerPoolerV2 would inappropriately bind a single-purpose dispatcher to an out-of-scope downstream contract.
original_severity: low (tentative; econ-scanner suggested promotion to Medium only if deployment broadcast cannot be ordered atomically — broadcast script is OOS).
summary:
Each migrateMint call increases NFTMinterV2._totalSupply[6] by `amount` with no on-chain economic backing on the dispatcher side. The protocol's claim of 'economic neutrality' across migration depends on a separate owner broadcast (migration plan step 11) minting fresh phUSD into NFTStakerV2 to extend its forward runway. If broadcast order is reversed (migration opens before staker top-up), early migrators stake into an underfunded staker and capture a disproportionate share of the eventual top-up via MasterChef-style accrual semantics.

Full original analysis preserved in /home/justin/code/C4/solidity-audit/reports/yield-claim-nft/07/audit/findings/raw-econ/ECON-RAW-009.json. The economic logic is sound but the responsibility lies outside this submodule.
